newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: KLASCO continues slide on dull Lithuanian bourse.
newsitem.headline: KLASCO continues slide on dull Lithuanian bourse.

text.p: Lithuania's sleepy bourse remained in the doldrums on Wednesday and dealers were not very bullish about the market's immediate prospects.
Shares have been easing steadily since a bull run in January pushed prices to record highs.
Dealers and analysts say that run was speculative and that the market has been undergoing a long and painful correction since.
The session's losers included state-run Klaipeda Stevedoring Company (KLASCO), which extended its recent slide, easing almost ten percent to 10.05 litas in trade of almost 60,000 litas.

Dealers said KLASCO's losses were a normal market response to its recent announcement that it planned to double its share capital from internal reserves and that its price probably would not fall much more.
"It looks like KLASCO has reached its market price ahead of the capital increase and should bottom out soon," said one dealer.
Most banking shares eased or remained steady.
Hermis Bank fell to 175.00 litas from 180.00 in trade of almost 22,000 litas.
The bank earlier announced that its net profit for April was 3.2 million litas and that its forecast for 1997 was 40.6 million litas.
Dealers said the market might not respond to the results in its current subdued mood but that its price was almost sure to rise when things picked up steam again.
